content:
deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy (mini-ramp) for prod-usw2
Environment: prod-usw2
Tag: release-2026-03-18-spark-canary
Commit: b3f7d9e
Targets: 5% traffic to canary, 5 nodes
Notes: includes kvcache tweak + kernel selection fallback
\nanna: ack, watching smoke tests :eyes:
\nraj: quick Q — is this using the new kv-prefetch flag or the fallback path? was supposed to be gated
\ndeploy-bot: rollout config: {"kvcache_mode":"prefetch_if_available","batcher":"adaptive"}
\nraj: ok, thanks. prefetched path enabled — keep an eye on mem pressure
\nsylvie: starting basic perf probes against canary: latency p95 baseline ~ 180ms
\nops-oncall: oncall: I have tracing open, will watch for RPC spikes. ping me if errors > 0.5% for 2 minutes
\ndeploy-bot: Canary reached 5% — smoke checks running (smoke-suite v2.4)
\nanna: logs show one transient 502 on a single node ~30s ago, retry cleared
\nraj: that 502 was the prefetch warmup, looks like cache miss backfill. CPU spiked 15% on that node
\nsylvie: perf probe: p95 now 190ms (+10ms), token throughput steady, error rate 0.08% across canary
\nops-oncall: no alerts triggered. error budget usage minimal
\nanna: running quick eval on 40 prompt samples — 1 regression flagged (formatting). small but logged
\nrelease-manager: copy of flagged sample? want to decide promo vs hold
\nanna: pasted sample in #eng-runtime with diffs, looks like deterministic tokenizer boundary change — not user-facing for most cases
\nraj: tagging that as low severity. I recommend continue to 20% and keep the eval set running at scale
\nrelease-manager: ok plan: promote to 20% now, wait 8 minutes, re-evaluate latency + regressions, then decide 50%/100%
\ndeploy-bot: Promoting canary to 20% target now — new target nodes: 12
\ndeploy-bot: Deploy event: promote -> 20% | tag: release-2026-03-18-spark-canary | commit: b3f7d9e
\nsylvie: mid-check: p95 185ms, p99 260ms, errors 0.09% — no new sample regressions in eval window
\nops-oncall: tracing shows slightly higher tail on 2 AZs, investigating network queueing, but impact isolated
\nanna: re-run smoke + eval, no new failures in last 6 minutes
\nraj: I still see memory on node canary-7 a bit high, but GC reclaimed — not sustained
\nrelease-manager: consensus: safe to step to 50% now, but pin the release tag to release/stable-candidate-2026-03-18 for rollback safety
\ndeploy-bot: Pinning tag: release/stable-candidate-2026-03-18 -> commit b3f7d9e
\ndeploy-bot: Promoting canary to 50% (staged) — will monitor for 12 minutes
\nops-oncall: enabling synthetic traffic at low rate across regions to stress tail latency
\nsylvie: after synthetic run: p95 190ms, p99 290ms, a single 504 from upstream dependency in eu-west region — unrelated
\nanna: eval set shows formatting regression still present in 1/40 samples, low severity. created ticket INF-4829 with repro
\nraj: preparing quick rollback playbook but holding since metrics look within SLOs
\nrelease-manager: decision: promote to 100% in 10 minutes unless new anomalies. notify #eng-releases when promote starts
\ndeploy-bot: Starting final promotion window -> target 100% in 10m unless hold
\nops-oncall: will page if error >0.5% sustained or latency +30% from baseline
\nsylvie: final check at T+9m: p95 188ms, p99 275ms, errors 0.12% — ok
\nanna: ok from me. release notes draft: "Kernel selection fallback and kvcache prefetch improvements; minor tokenizer boundary change noted (INF-4829)."
\nrelease-manager: promoting to 100% now. tagging: v1.14.2
\ndeploy-bot: Promotion complete. Environment: prod-usw2 -> 100% traffic
Tag applied: v1.14.2
Commit: b3f7d9e
Duration: 32m total (mini-ramp)
\nops-oncall: monitoring continuing for 1h. so far stable :thumbsup:
\nraj: leaving rollback playbook on standby. if we need to roll back: rollout -> pin previous tag release-2026-03-10-stable and scale down canary nodes
\nrelease-manager: closing note: great coordination. I'll add the change window summary to the release doc and link INF-4829. Thanks team :tada:
